newsitem.title: PANAMA: Foreign airlines resume partial service in Panama.
newsitem.headline: Foreign airlines resume partial service in Panama.

text.p: Foreign airlines partially resumed service on Thursday at Panama's Tocumen International Airport after a crippling strike by air traffic controllers.
"We're grateful to be able to get limited service going again," American Airlines spokeswoman Andrea Rader told Reuters from their corporate offices in Dallas, Texas.

She said American would fly under a contingency plan adopted by Panamanian authorities using air traffic controllers from the United States during peak international traffic hours. "For the moment we feel safe under that plan."
Officials of Continental Airlines, KLM of the Netherlands and Taiwan's Eva Air also said they would resume partial service.

At least 49 of 94 striking air traffic controllers were dismissed after they stopped work on Tuesday demanding better pay and pension benefits. Government officials estimate the strike cost Panama about $3 million in airline ticket and cargo sales.
President Ernesto Perez Balladares backed the decision to fire the controllers and said they would not be rehired.

The controllers walked out after talks on a pay hike to $2,000 monthly from an average of $600 monthly broke down over the weekend. They also want a package allowing them to retire earlier than the national average of 62 years for men and 57 years for women.
